title: Favorite players by instrument: trombone, piano, drums, saxes, banjo, bass
summary: Howard names the New Orleans players he admired and instrumentation then in use.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Who were some of the other trombone players that you liked?
Oh Jim, Sonny, all of them. Sonny? Sonny, yeah. Sonny's great.
Albert.
Which Sonny though? Sonny Henry. Sonny Henry. Albert Warner. Yank, his brother Buddy. Johnson. Yeah, Buddy Johnson, all of them. Bill. Yeah, Bill, yeah. Matthews.
Matthews. I see.
During that time, Bill was with Papa Sellers, they in the big band.
Did you hear many piano players then?

Well yeah, they had piano players then. Pop had, I don't know, I think Jeanette was working with him. She was working with Pops. Well they had a good many piano players. Ben Ateno, he played with Pops too. Moisey D, Phil, you know Moisey D. But she worked with me a long time.
These were all good piano players. Yeah, yeah. Good. Did you listen to anybody on drums much when you got started to learn from them?

Well they had some real good drummers. Roy was really terrific. Alfred, he's great. Who? Alfred Williams. I used to hear Black Benny, Ray Happy, was that the lyrics? Uh-huh. Oh, a good many of them. They was good drummers.
What about saxophone players in those days? When did that come in?

Well, Earl was great. Earl Fuscher. He was tough and handy. Son Johnson, them people. Who does Son Johnson work with now? I wouldn't know where he'd work or anything about Son. I haven't heard from Son in so many years. Nothing about him.
What about banjo and guitar? Do they have any great banjo and guitar players now?
Well, Gael and Johnny Davis to play with Sam, Percy, and oh.
Percy which?
I just remember this guy.
Is he in Natchez the one?
Yeah, that one.
Percy Severe.
Percy Severe, that's right. The wife used to play too, yeah.
What did she play? Badge?
Yeah?
I didn't know that.
Well, all those was Thomas. Joel Moreira. And Lawrence, the brother. Guitar? Who would play guitar then?
Well, at that time it was banjo. Banjo was the thing? Banjo was the thing.
Were they using string bass or tubo when you started?
They were using string bass. And the band would use tubos. I mean, like Lil Jim, when he could double. But he used to double with Sam.

Or string bass? He'd have wanted to know. Well, Ransom was a great bass player. He used to play with Sidney Desvien. Harmon Mitchell, we used to call him Basie. He used to call him Basie. And he used to play with Sidney Desvien. And the band would use tubos. I mean, like Lil Jim, when he could double. But he used to double with Sam. Who else would be a good tuba player then? Or string bass? He'd have wanted to know. Well, Ransom was a great bass player. He used to play with Sidney Desvien.
Harmon Mitchell, we used to call him Basie. That was a short fella.
He played both good, because when Eddie died, he'd taken Eddie with us in the tuxedo, brass band, to play the big horn. And he was good.
